key_insight: Scalable modal decomposition reveals dominant coherent flow structures and their temporal dynamics around a Formula 1 front wing while compressing approximately 6 TB of snapshots into 200 GB of modal data.
engineering_relevance: Identifying characteristic frequencies of wing-flow instabilities can support aerodynamic diagnosis and reduced-order modeling for motorsport design.
method: Simulate the Imperial Front Wing at Re = 2.2 × 10^5 using spectral/hp-element LES in Nektar++.
Apply scalable POD and DMD through the open-source pyLOM framework.
Use point-probe spectra to associate DMD modes with specific flow mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The simulation uses 49.72 million degrees of freedom, reports lift and drag coefficient differences of 2.24% and 2.87% from reference data, and links chord-based Strouhal numbers 5.1, 7.5 and 9.3 to distinct flow mechanisms.
watch_item: The abstract demonstrates one geometry and Reynolds number; transferability to other operating conditions and reduced-order predictive accuracy remain unestablished.
paper_title: Scalable Modal Analysis of the Imperial Front Wing Flow Field
